name: phoronix-test-suite
desc: Open-source automated testing/benchmarking software
why: Automated benchmarking framework with a large test library, a niche but somewhat familiar tool.

name: redka
desc: Redis re-implemented with SQLite
why: Redis protocol reimplemented on SQLite is a strange, appealing database twist worth a look.

name: unuran
desc: UNU.RAN - Universal Non-Uniform RANdom number generator
why: A serious random-variate generator library for arbitrary distributions, a real mathematical tool with obscure appeal.

name: luajit
desc: Just-In-Time Compiler (JIT) for the Lua programming language
why: A famously fast JIT for Lua with a fascinating internals story, but widely used and somewhat familiar.

name: direwolf
desc: Software "soundcard" AX.25 packet modem/TNC and APRS encoder/decoder
why: A software soundcard turning audio into AX.25 packets and APRS, a delightful audio-to-data transform you can hear.

name: tinc
desc: Virtual Private Network (VPN) tool
why: A mesh VPN daemon with an unusual decentralised design, a fair door into tunnelling protocols.

name: wumpus
desc: Exact clone of the ancient BASIC Hunt the Wumpus game
why: An exact clone of the original BASIC Hunt the Wumpus, a classic and strange piece of computing history.

name: chipmunk-physics
desc: 2D rigid body physics library written in C
why: A compact 2D rigid body physics engine is a real simulation door, though it is a library and more plumbing than spectacle.

name: coordgen
desc: Schrodinger-developed 2D Coordinate Generation
why: Chemistry 2D coordinate generation is a niche scientific library, interesting in its domain but mostly a component to link against.

name: onioncat
desc: VPN-adapter that provides location privacy using Tor or I2P
why: Turning Tor or I2P into a VPN adapter with IPv6-derived addresses is a clever door into how overlay networks route traffic.

name: fossil
desc: Distributed software configuration management
why: A git alternative bundling wiki, tickets and web UI in one SQLite file; a genuinely odd design worth a look.

name: fernflower
desc: Advanced decompiler for Java bytecode
why: JetBrains' Java bytecode decompiler; a real window into reconstructing source from compiled classes.

name: chrony
desc: Versatile implementation of the Network Time Protocol (NTP)
why: Alternative NTP implementation; a door into time sync that runs everywhere but is rarely examined.

name: dex2jar
desc: Tools to work with Android .dex and Java .class files
why: Converts Android dex bytecode into Java jars, opening up APKs for inspection and poking.

name: stackql
desc: SQL interface for arbitrary resources with full CRUD support
why: Treats cloud resources as SQL tables; an unusual abstraction worth a short poke.

name: bossa
desc: Flash utility for Atmel SAM microcontrollers
why: Flashes firmware onto Atmel SAM boards; a hands-on hardware tool, close call on interest.

name: klee
desc: Symbolic Execution Engine
why: Symbolic execution engine that finds inputs driving programs down hidden paths; a strange and rewarding way to watch code think.

name: pawk
desc: Python line processor (like AWK)
why: A Python-flavoured take on AWK's line processing; a mild curiosity that shows awk's idea transplanted into another language.

name: minica
desc: Small, simple certificate authority
why: A tiny certificate authority that is a clean, readable door into how TLS trust and certificates are issued.

name: cvs
desc: Version control system
why: A pre-git version control system, a fossil of how teams once shared code, worth a look for history.

name: libnfc
desc: Low level NFC SDK and Programmers API
why: A low-level NFC SDK that lets you talk to readers and tags directly, a real door into contactless protocols.

name: libpst
desc: Utilities for the PST file format
why: Utilities for decoding Outlook PST files let you dig into a proprietary, obscure file format.

name: msolve
desc: Library for Polynomial System Solving through Algebraic Methods
why: A serious computer algebra solver for polynomial systems that you can run at home on real math problems.

name: trzsz
desc: Simple file transfer tools, similar to lrzsz (rz/sz), and compatible with tmux
why: A modern take on rz/sz that moves files through the terminal stream, a window into the old ZMODEM-style transfer idea.

name: norm
desc: NACK-Oriented Reliable Multicast
why: NACK-oriented reliable multicast is an obscure transport protocol, and this is a real implementation to explore.
